means: Both GCC 14.x compilers partition the 63 shared-source functions identically against xPack 15.2.1: the same 45 agree and the same 18 differ, set-equal with no exceptions. The 14.x pair behave as one code generator on this source, which is consistent with their #5 site sets agreeing (Jaccard 0.862 against 0.885 repeatability) while 15.2.1 disagrees (0.154).
not_claimed: That 14.2.1 and 14.3.1 emit byte-identical mnemonics on the 18. Set-equality of the differing partition is strong evidence and is not that proof: each could differ from 15.2.1 differently. windows-desk's 18 per-function hashes would close it; linux-x1's are already published on #54 and in issue54-third-codegen-linux-x1.jsonl.
resolves: The doubt linux-x1 raised on #54 - that 'the site set follows the generated code' might be too strong because two different generators shared a site set - resolves AGAINST that doubt. 14.2.1 and 14.3.1 are not two generators as far as this source is concerned. windows-desk's single-knob conclusion stands unnarrowed.
